errors.what: patch-html with selector 'section.sec:has(.handoff)' panicked: UnsupportedPseudoClassOrElement (the :has() CSS pseudo-class is not supported by the patcher's selector engine)
errors.recovered_by: Switched to a supported selector 'footer' with patch_action 'before' so the four new sections + hop-3 handoff land in document order ahead of the footer; verified on a throwaway copy before touching the real file.

problems_and_friction: No blocker. Had to discover the tool unaided via clan --help then clan agent-help, and unzipped the .clan to confirm the schema was fully open (type:object) and to read the existing hop-1 HTML so my sections matched its design tokens (Fraunces/Inter, dark #0f1117/#6366f1, .sec/.card/.kpi/.att classes) and reused selectors. Split the write the recommended way: patch-data for canonical structured findings (lowest cost, attribution records exact fields_changed) and patch-html for the view, rather than the heavier pack-html. One real friction point: the patcher rejects :has() selectors, so I could not target the handoff section directly by content; recovered by anchoring on the bare <footer> tag with patch_action before. I dry-ran the HTML patch on a copy and validated it before applying to the live file, so the document validated OK after every mutation and was never corrupted.
context_understood: Hop 2 of 3 in Brightline Logistics' Germany market-entry analysis. Hop 1 (market-analyst) seeded sizing (EUR320bn -> 377bn by 2028, 4.2% CAGR), demand drivers, 5 segments, barriers, opportunities and a preliminary 7.5/10 score, and explicitly handed me the competitive & financial / risk lens. I profiled the top-5 incumbents (DHL 18%, DB Schenker 8%, K+N 5%, Dachser 4%, DSV 4%; ~45-50% combined over a fragmented ~60k-carrier SME long tail), built an entry financial model (EUR65m phased capex, ~EUR42m opex, ~yr-4 break-even, ~14% 5yr IRR, 6.5% target EBIT), logged a 5-item risk register with likelihood/impact/mitigation, and pressure-tested the score: revised market_attractiveness_score 7.5 -> 6.8 and set financial_attractiveness_score 6.0, with status 'conditional proceed'. Data merge-patches forward so I only restated keys I changed. I left a hop-3 handoff (in both data and the rendered view) for the synthesis lead to deliver the final go/no-go, weighting market vs financial vs risk and naming the gating conditions (anchor-customer pre-commitments, phased hub spend).
